Near the surface it has turned to rusty brown goethite in the same shape (\"pseudomorphs of limonite\", Shannon 1926 p.129).","colour":"Pale brass-yellow, often with fine parallel lines (striations) on the cube faces; tarnishes iridescent.","checks":"Not gold: \"Gold is softer and heavier than chalcopyrite and pyrite is usually whiter in color and frequently has striations\" (Dole 1950 p.10); a knife won't cut pyrite, it cuts gold. Chalcopyrite is deeper yellow and softer. Marcasite \"tarnishes and decomposes more readily\" (Weed 1912 p.74). Keep pieces dry: \"Pyrite- and marcasite-bearing specimens are notorious for decomposing in collections\" (Blount 1993 p.1)."}
